name: Samuel Tak Lee
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Samuel Tak Lee owns property company Langham Estate, which manages a swath of prime retail and office space in London's West End.
Lee reportedly sold part of his 1.3 million-square-foot property portfolio in the West End for £340 million ($430 million) in 2024.
His property holdings also stretch from Hong Kong to Geneva.
In 2020, Lee sold his entire stake in London-based Shaftesbury, a publicly traded real estate company, at a discount for $589 million.
forbes_facts: In 2015, Lee donated $118 million to his alma mater the Massachusetts Institute of Technology to establish a real estate entrepreneurship lab.

name: Sanjiv Goenka
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Sanjiv Goenka controls the $4.9 billion (revenue) conglomerate RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group, headquartered in Kolkata.
Its flagship is 127-year-old power utility, CESC, which Goenka has restructured into four separate companies.
Other assets include supermarket chain Spencer's and snacks brand Too Yumm!, which son Shashwat looks after.
Goenka has the franchise for Indian Premier League cricket team, Lucknow Super Giants. In 2025, he bought 70% of U.K. cricket team, Manchester Originals.
forbes_facts: His older brother Harsh Goenka, who runs his separate group, is also a billionaire.
Goenka's private property portfolio includes a bungalow in Delhi's exclusive Lutyens zone.

name: Lorenzo Fertitta
sec_insider_companies: Red Rock Resorts, Inc. (RRR) - Vice President
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Lorenzo Fertitta and his brother, Frank, made the bulk of their fortune through mixed martial arts promoter UFC.
They bought UFC for $2 million in 2001; an investment group led by WME/IMG bought it for $4 billion in 2016.
They sold their remaining stakes in UFC in August 2017 at a $5 billion valuation.
The Fertittas took public their casino business, Red Rock Resorts, in 2016. It was founded by their father.
They each pledged $7.5 million in 2016 to NYU's Stern School of Business for a scholarship for veterans.
forbes_facts: The Fertittas got hooked on martial arts after taking weekly lessons in their casino's basement. In 2001, they bought UFC, owning it until a 2016 sale to WME-IMG.
Fertitta's son Nicco played safety for the University of Notre Dame football team and is now an assistant coach at UNLV.

name: Ren Yuanlin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2007-2026)
forbes_bio: Ren Yuanlin chairs Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, one of China's largest shipyards.
Ren joined the company in the1970s, then called Jiangyin Shipbuilding Factory, and headed its ship body workshop. He worked his way up to a factory supervisor and eventually became chairman in 1997.
In 2022, Yangzijiang Financial Holding, a former subsidiary, spun off from the group and went public in Singapore.
Apart from Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, Ren's wealth also includes his stake in Yangzijiang Financial and debt investments.

name: Jamie Dimon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Jamie Dimon runs JPMorgan Chase, the largest bank in the U.S. in terms of assets.
Dimon, a Harvard Business School grad, began his finance career at American Express in 1982 and later helped build the modern day Citigroup.
He has been CEO of JPMorgan Chase since 2006 and chairman since 2007.
His move to unload $12 billion of subprime mortgages in 2006 buffered his bank against the 2008 crash.
Dimon was rumored to be a candidate for treasury secretary under Donald Trump in both 2016 and 2024, and he sat on Trump's policy forum until it was disbanded in 2017.
forbes_facts: His Greek grandfather worked at Bank of Athens and changed the family name from Papademetriou to Dimon.
Dimon was diagnosed with throat cancer in 2014, took time off work in 2015 after receiving treatment and then returned to work full time.

name: Glen Taylor
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Glen Taylor bought a wedding service business for $2 million in 1975 and turned it into Taylor Corp., a printing firm with over $2 billion in sales.
Taylor, who worked at the wedding business throughout college, stepped down as CEO of Taylor Corp. in 2015; he remains chairman.
A Minnesotan, Taylor owns stakes in the state's NBA team, the Timberwolves; WNBA team, the  Lynx; and the United FC soccer team.
In 2016, he sold 5% of his stake in both basketball teams to Lizhang Jiang, the NBA's first Chinese minority owner.
Taylor also owns farmland in Minnesota and Iowa, as well as the Minneapolis Star Tribune, which he bought in 2014 for nearly $100 million.
forbes_facts: Taylor grew up poor on a farm in southern Minnesota.
As a kid he worked on his neighbors' farms for $1 an hour.

name: Peter Unger
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: From a single location opened in 1985, Peter Unger built his namesake auto parts and repair outfit Auto-Teile-Unger (A.T.U.) into a nationwide chain.
In 2002, he sold 72% of the company for $900 million to Doughty Hanson & Co. Two years later, he sold his remaining stake for $360 million to KKR & Co.
Residing in Bavaria, Unger now invests in listed companies, startups and both residential and commercial real estate throughout Germany.
Investments include food hygiene company aquagroup, a bike center focused on electric bicycles, and sensor technology startup Tacerion.
forbes_facts: In Berlin, where he also has commercial real estate, Unger has either purchased or invested in the construction of thousands of apartments with partner Groth Gruppe.

name: Guenther Lehmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2014-2020); Hurun Global (2015-2023)
forbes_bio: Guenther Lehmann's family owns 50% of Germany's leading drugstore chain, dm (drogerie markt), which brings in around $12 billion in annual revenue.
The company got its start in 1973 when Goetz Werner opened his first shop in Karlsruhe, Germany.
The following year, Lehmann, then running his family's Pfannkuch grocery chain, invested in dm.
Little is known about Lehmann, who has not been operationally involved in dm, and his family.
forbes_facts: Werner transferred his 50% of dm to a charitable foundation. His son Christoph, a member of dm's management board since 2011, now runs the company.
The dm philosophy, that ensuring employee well being brings greater long-term success for the company, is well-known in German-speaking countries.

name: Cai Jianyong
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023); Hurun China (2023-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Cai Jianyong chairs China nickel supplier Lygend Resources & Technology, headquartered on the coast of the East China Sea.
He founded the company in 2009, after nearly a decade in the commodities trading business.
Lygend trades and produces nickel products, essential for stainless steel and electric vehicle batteries.
Lygend went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in November 2022, raising money to expand its operations in Indonesia, home to much of the world's nickel resources.
Cai graduated from the Shanghai Institute of Building Materials Industry.

(GGT) - Director,Other; M-tron Industries, Inc. (MPTI) - TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Mario Gabelli runs Gamco, a mutual fund and investment firm he founded in 1977.
Gabelli's reputation for stock-picking took off in the 1980s, when he found success betting on the media and telecom sectors.
A first-generation college student, Gabelli graduated from Fordham University's business school, now named for him, in 1965.
He is a big donor to higher education and a signatory of the Giving Pledge.
He also serves as executive chairman of Associated Capital Group, an investment management business that spun off from Gamco in 2015.
forbes_facts: A life-long contrarian, even as a schoolboy Gabelli refused to hide with classmates during air raid drills.
Around age five, Gabelli set up a shoe-shine box at a Bronx subway station to make money. He bought his first stocks at 13 years old.

name: Luis Riu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Luis Riu is co-CEO of Riu Hotels & Resorts, which he owns with his sister Carmen Guell, also a billionaire.
The group, which operates 98 hotels in 21 countries, saw more than $4.5 billion in revenue and $150 million in net profit in 2024.
Riu oversees the company's operations and expansion, both for its urban hotels and its Caribbean resort stronghold.
He is a third-generation family member of the Riu hospitality empire, which he joined in the 1980s; he has since led its push into city hotels and all-inclusive luxury resorts.
Riu also invests in new-build hotel projects in Mexico, the U.S., and Cape Verde.
forbes_facts: Riu is said to personally scout and approve every international resort location before its construction.
He was instrumental in the group's entry into New York City's Times Square hotel market in 2010.
